clue.text: Foot child placed by line

parts.note: an infant is a young child
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A child's foot is set beside a ruler line for measuring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' looks like a body part or a measurement, but it means foot soldiers; 'placed by' only sets the two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Foot soldiers collectively are the army's infantry, so 'foot' is a military synonym.

clue.text: Small island in main channel

indicators.note: in shows the letters are found inside the words main channel

explanation.surface: A tiny island sits in the middle of a shipping channel.
explanation.walkthrough: An inch is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland and Ireland an inch is an islet, often in a firth or lake.

clue.text: Female I have made famous in books

parts.note: I've is the short form of I have

explanation.surface: A woman claims she has become a celebrated author.
explanation.walkthrough: The Famous Five are the child heroes of Enid Blyton's series of British children's books.
explanation.definitionFit: The number named in the title of Enid Blyton's Famous Five series is the one those books made famous.

clue.text: With cooking, men turn it into food

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are mixed up as ingredients are

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: When they cook, men turn it into a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nourishment that sustains the body is food.

clue.text: Motorist may be unable to see this cuckoo

definitions.text: Motorist may be unable to see this
definitions.meaning: a driver cannot see what lies beyond a curve in the road

explanation.surface: A driver may miss seeing a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Round a curve is hidden from view, and the phrase is also slang for insane.

clue.text: Parallel research's beginning in the subject

indicators.note: in places the opening letter inside the word for the subject

parts.note: a topic is the subject under discussion

indicators.note: beginning picks out only the opening letter of the word research's

explanation.surface: An academic notes how research begins with a parallel drawn in its subject.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are parallels of latitude, lines circling the globe.

clue.text: Provoke noisy arguments

indicators.note: noisy signals that the word is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: rows are noisy quarrels or arguments

explanation.surface: Loud arguments stir people up.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up or excite someone is to provoke them.

clue.text: Terms for food

definitions.meaning: the clauses or conditions in a contract

explanation.surface: Conditions laid down for eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Conditions in an agreement are its stipulations, and stocks of supplies are stores of food.

clue.text: Has let crew get drunk? They need to go on the wagon, perhaps

definitions.text: They need to go on the wagon, perhaps

indicators.note: drunk means the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A captain lets the crew get drunk, and then they must swear off drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go on the wagon' means give up alcohol, but here the wagon literally rolls on these.
explanation.definitionFit: A cart or wagon runs on wheels, so they must be fitted to it.

clue.text: Partners forbid us to become grasping

parts.note: CO, short for company, is a firm of partners
to veto something is to forbid it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Business partners ban us from becoming greedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone grasping is greedy and envious, longing for what others own.

clue.text: Grapevine produces this drink belonging to us

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
our means belonging to us

explanation.surface: A vine yields a drink that is ours to share.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grapevine' suggests wine, but here it is the gossip network, and what it passes on is unconfirmed talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearing something on the grapevine means picking up unverified gossip, which is what the grapevine spreads.

clue.text: Become agitated and burp

definitions.meaning: to bring up air, as one does to a baby after feeding

explanation.surface: Someone gets anxious and belches.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerves are shown by the idiom, while bringing up gas from the stomach is the literal sense.

clue.text: Aerial picture of plant to compete with

parts.note: bird's-eye is the name of several small-flowered plants, such as germander speedwell
to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: A photograph of a plant is entered in a competition.
explanation.definitionFit: A view from high above, as a bird sees it, is an overhead or aerial picture.

clue.text: Instructor's equipment to get on jet first

indicators.note: first says the jet piece comes ahead of the boarding piece

parts.note: jet is a deep black colour
to board a vehicle is to get on it

explanation.surface: Equipment for an instructor needs to be loaded before the jet takes off.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher writes on this chalk surface at the front of a classroom.

clue.text: Landing after taking flight from here

definitions.text: Landing after taking flight from here

parts.words: Landing after taking flight from here
parts.note: a flight is a set of stairs, and you go down it from the landing to reach the lower floor

explanation.surface: A plane lands after taking off from here.
explanation.definitionFit: Descending a flight of stairs brings one to the floor below.

clue.text: Heads East fast

parts.note: heads are toilets in naval slang, and loos are toilets in British slang

explanation.surface: People turn eastward and move quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' is the naval word for toilets, LOOS in everyday British English; 'fast' is the old sense of dissolute, as in a fast woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast in the sense of wild and immoral living matches loose, as in loose morals.

clue.text: Thumb knot needed to pull

parts.note: a hitch is a kind of knot
to hike something up is to pull it up

explanation.surface: A thumb is tied in a knot that needs a tug.
explanation.definitionFit: To thumb a lift is to travel by flagging down drivers, a colloquial verb for roadside lift-cadging.

clue.text: How to make one horse obscure and unimportant

definitions.text: How to make one horse obscure and unimportant

parts.words: How to make one horse obscure and unimportant
parts.note: joining words with dashes makes a compound such as one-horse, meaning small and insignificant

explanation.surface: Instructions for making a horse seem forgettable.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-horse town is small and unimportant; the phrase only works when joined with a dash.
explanation.definitionFit: Linking words with a dash makes them a single compound term.

clue.text: He may have to sort out stolen cab

definitions.text: He may have to sort out stolen cab

indicators.note: to sort out is to put in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, part of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A police officer may have to deal with a stolen taxi.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer is the person who would deal with a theft such as a stolen cab.

clue.text: Where instruments are set out for doctors

definitions.meaning: the dials and gauges in a car or aircraft are mounted on a board
a body of doctors, such as those on a list available to patients

explanation.surface: Somewhere surgical instruments are laid out for physicians.
explanation.definitionFit: An instrument board is a panel, and a group of experts or doctors is also a panel.

clue.text: Occasionally, when you read the Sunday papers?

definitions.text: Occasionally, when you read the Sunday papers?

parts.words: Occasionally, when you read the Sunday papers?
parts.note: the Sunday papers come out on the day when this newspaper, the Times, does not, so you read them in the gaps between issues

explanation.surface: Someone reads the weekend papers only now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The Times was not published on Sunday, so Sunday papers are read in the interval separating two issues of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Now and then, in the intervals, is the idiomatic sense of occasionally.

clue.text: Shove and half-heartedly shake up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read upwards, so the word is reversed
half the heart is lost: one of the two middle letters goes

parts.note: to wobble is to shake

explanation.surface: Push and give it a feeble shake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of WOBBLE's two central Bs, leaving WOBLE; 'up' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To push someone aside with your arm is to shove them.

clue.text: Discover nude finally getting out of the buff

indicators.note: getting out of means a letter leaves the word for buff

parts.note: a buff is an enthusiast, a fiend for something

indicators.note: finally picks out only the last letter of nude

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a naked person stripping off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the buff' means naked, so 'nude' and 'buff' seem to belong together; here a buff is an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something is to discover it.

clue.text: Stable boss

definitions.meaning: an establishment where horses are kept for breeding
a knob or raised ornament on a surface

explanation.surface: The head of a riding stable.
explanation.definitionFit: A breeding establishment for horses and a projecting knob are both the same word.

clue.text: Going into a stunning blow, one doctor shows how arms may be positioned

definitions.text: shows how arms may be positioned

indicators.note: going into places one piece inside another

parts.note: A plus KO, a knockout, a blow that stuns
I is the Roman numeral for one
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor punched senseless demonstrates where to put one's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Arms held with hands on hips and elbows out are said to be in that position.

clue.text: Thought programme romantic

parts.note: an idea is a thought
a list of items is a programme or schedule

explanation.surface: A thoughtful programme with a romantic theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic person pursues lofty ideals rather than practical realities, a near synonym.

clue.text: Deny one's covered with feathers

indicators.note: one piece is covered by another, so it goes inside

parts.note: down is a bird's soft feathers
I for one plus S, so one's gives I and S

explanation.surface: Someone denies being covered in feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: To renounce or refuse to acknowledge someone is to deny any link with them.

clue.text: I had, in advance, to fork out about a pound fine

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around another

parts.note: to fork out is to spend money
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra
I'd is the short form of I had

explanation.surface: Someone had to pay out about a pound in advance and thought it fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in advance, to' is surface padding; the pieces simply run in the order of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendid and fine are both terms of approval meaning excellent.
